related_questions.question: Was there a population decline due to COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, the US population did experience a temporary decline during the COVID-19 pandemic. This was primarily due to increased mortality rates and a decrease in fertility rates. The pandemic's impact on mortality, fertility, and immigration resulted in a roughly 0.5% reduction in the US population, according to the Penn Wharton Budget Model.

list.title: Increased Mortality:
list.snippet: The pandemic caused a significant spike in deaths, particularly among older populations, contributing to a decrease in the overall population.

list.title: Decreased Fertility:
list.snippet: Birth rates also declined during the pandemic, as couples delayed or decided against having children due to economic uncertainty and other pandemic-related factors.

list.title: Disrupted Immigration:
list.snippet: The pandemic also led to disruptions in immigration patterns, further impacting population growth.

text_blocks.snippet: While the mortality rate has since diminished, the low fertility rates persist, and deaths still exceed births in many regions, according to the Carsey School of Public Policy.
